data.narrative:
44.01 is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Talal Hasan that has raised $37M to date. The valuation landscape in Climate & Energy includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers spanning technologies from energy storage to advanced materials and minerals processing.

Valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, given insufficient narrow-peer clustering to support a reliable peer-median approach. The Climate & Energy sector has eight private companies in the comp universe, but none yielded three or more datapoints at the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—the minimum threshold for meaningful peer triangulation. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier from the $37M total raised proxy, a typical Series A-to-subsequent-round expansion factor, yielding an implied valuation of $74M.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, with a median of $74M. The range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression anchor, acknowledging that a single-method conclusion carries higher uncertainty than multi-method triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables at the same stage and the reliance on a raised-capital proxy rather than post-money terms. A peer-median approach would strengthen conviction if additional same-stage Climate & Energy companies enter the dataset.
